subject: [PATCH] x86/mm: Fix pmd_modify() dropping the dirty bit

reviews.author: Dave Hansen
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dave Hansen expressed skepticism about the explicit exclusion of _PAGE_DIRTY from the mask in pmd_modify(), attributing it to a remnant from an earlier patch version, and questioned its asymmetry with pte_modify(). He acknowledged that the fix itself is correct but noted that it has been causing data loss for users who combine huge pages with MADV_FREE.
reviews.raw_body:
My guess is that it's some remnant from an earlier version of the patch.
The asymmetry with pte_modify() vs. pmd_modify() just can't be explained
any other way. It _might_ have been some attempt to say, "Hey
_PAGE_DIRTY is now a part of the pgprot_t since it's part of the
'permissions' of a shadow stack PTE" that got abandoned.

But I don't see anything wrong with the fix at all.

It does give me pause that this has been losing user data for so long,
but it must just be a weird combination of features that few folks use
together (huge pages + MADV_FREE).

reviews.author: Edgecombe, P
reviews.summary: Reviewer Edgecombe, P noted that the patch's pmd_modify() function did not update its mask adjustment to handle the dirty bit correctly, which was previously handled separately in the mkdirty helpers.

2026-09-03.patch_summary: This patch fixes an issue in the x86/mm code where the pmd_modify() function was dropping the dirty bit when modifying page table entries. The problem arose from a mask that excluded the _PAGE_DIRTY flag, which is corrected by changing the mask to include it. This ensures that the dirty bit is preserved during modifications.
